meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'помнить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remember, to recall', paired with 'вспоминать'.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'mouth' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Самсонов, рот закрой! Зачем ты его обижаешь?
examples.trans: Samsonov, shut your mouth! Why are you insulting him?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'grand' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They paid good money for that menu.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to pay', paired with 'заплатить'.

examples.text: А вашу работу вернуть можно. И мы хорошо платим.
examples.trans: But we can get your job back for you. And we pay well.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Разговорчики, лейтенант Соколов! Быстро на рабочее место.
examples.trans: That's enough talk, Lieutenant Sokolov! Back to your desk, quickly.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

успеть.gloss: to make it, to be in time

meanings.en: to make it, to be in time
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to make it, to be in time', paired with 'успевать'.

examples.trans: We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

examples.text: Ты успела отправить видео?! Зачем ты это сделала?
examples.trans: You managed to send the video?! Why did you do that?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hour' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let's go'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?
Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.
All right, let's go to our room.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'over there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сюда').

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to decide, to solve', paired with 'решить'.

examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

examples.text: Вот он, телефон! Сами решайте, что делать. Без меня!
examples.trans: Here it is, the phone! Decide for yourselves what to do. Without me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

examples.text: Хорошо. Значит, вот куда идут деньги налогоплательщиков.
examples.trans: Fine. So this is where taxpayers' money goes.

examples.text: Значит, вот куда идут деньги налогоплательщиков.
examples.trans: So this is where taxpayers' money goes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'little one, kid' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Послушай, малыш, у меня есть деловое предложение.
examples.trans: Listen, kid, I've got a business proposal.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'куска'). Common feminine noun meaning 'appetizer, snack' in everyday Russian.
